title: Freya and the Crown
premise: Ulyana Pemberton, last apprentice of the Charmwrights' Guild, has survived two decades of the godless republic by selling trinkets that no longer work—until the old gods begin answering prayers again, and every charm Ulyana ever sold starts waking up. Hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking and guided by a ragtag found family of former clients and heretics, they must locate the Door of Ash, the only passage out of Vessia, a country that was officially erased from maps twenty years ago. The gods are returning not to save anyone but to reclaim their debts, and Ulyana's own name is the final payment. In the end, Ulyana chooses to stay: they rewrite the debt into an inheritance, becoming not a servant of the gods but the mortal keeper of the Door, holding it open for everyone else while finally claiming a name, a family, and a country of their own making.
about_author: Noor Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated folk charms in Eastern European museum basements. They write fantasy about bureaucracy, belief, and the people history forgets to erase.

chapters.title: The Trinket That Bled
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Selling charms in the night market of a city that outlawed magic, Ulyana notices one old piece weeping rust-colored light—a love charm from twenty years ago working again. A Ministry inspector nearly catches them; a stranger named Brannic buys the charm and whispers that prayers are being answered. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a dangerous flicker of hope.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Retracing two decades of sales, Ulyana finds every charm they ever made has reawakened—and each carries a fragment of a different god's attention. Their landlady Sefa, a former client, reveals she prayed for her sick grandson using Ulyana's charm, and he recovered. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Ministry of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. A former Ministry clerk, Brannic explains the republic didn't just ban magic—it legally dissolved Vessia itself, erasing the nation so the gods would starve without believers. Now the Ministry hunts 'residual practitioners.' Ulyana's guild records have surfaced. Emotional beat: cold institutional terror rendered intimate through Brannic's complicity and shame.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Raiding the sealed guildhall, Ulyana finds their master's ledger: the Charmwrights never made charms—they made payments, and the guild's extinction was a deliberate default on a divine contract. Ulyana's apprenticeship was collateral. Emotional beat: identity shattered; everything they built was a debt instrument.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled Badly
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third POVs. Sefa, Brannic, a defrocked Ministry cartographer named Ivo, and a teenage pickpocket who owns Ulyana's luckiest charm gather in Sefa's kitchen. They argue, feed each other, and form a plan to find the Door of Ash before the Ministry does. Emotional beat: warmth forged from mutual desperation.

chapters.title: The Map That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The cartographer's erased maps show Vessia only when drawn in blood-ink mixed with prayer. Following the ghost-borders, the group crosses countryside where villages remember being part of a country that officially never existed. Ministry trackers close in. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland that exists only in stubborn memory.

chapters.title: Prayer as Weapon
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cornered at a border shrine, Ulyana prays for the first time in twenty years—and the god who answers is the one their master defaulted on. It offers a bargain: Ulyana's name and service in exchange for the others' safe passage. Ulyana refuses, buying time with a counter-charm that burns half their craft-memory away. Emotional beat: defiance at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Door of Ash
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The group reaches the Door—a hearth in a ruined village church that opens onto everywhere Vessia used to be. But it demands a keeper, and the Ministry arrives with the god's herald at its head. Sefa's grandson, healed by Ulyana's charm, unknowingly holds the key: gratitude freely given. Emotional beat: ordinary love revealed as the strongest magic left.

chapters.title: The Debt Rewritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV (climax). Before the Door, Ulyana offers the god a new contract: not servitude, but stewardship—the guild reborn as keepers of the Door, paid in worship freely chosen rather than owed. The god, starving for genuine belief rather than coerced payment, accepts. The Ministry's authority collapses when its own clerks pray. Emotional beat: triumph through negotiation, not violence.

chapters.title: A Country of One's Own
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV (resolution). Months later, the Door stands open in a rebuilt guildhall; refugees, believers, and the found family pass through freely. Ulyana signs the new ledger—not Pemberton, the inherited name, but a name they chose—and teaches the first new apprentice. Vessia exists again, on nobody's map but its own. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
